_comment: Single source of truth for every value two or more implementations must agree on.
node scripts/protocol.js gen writes desktop_hub/protocol.gen.js (Node) and
android .../core/crypto/ProtocolConst.kt (Kotlin) from this file; node scripts/protocol.js check
regenerates them in memory and fails on any difference, additionally asserting that the
hand-written browser literals (public/app.js, public/portal.html and its byte-identical copy in
the Android assets) still match, because a self-contained portal page cannot import a module.
Only interop-critical values belong here. Single-implementation tuning (the Android socket read
timeout, the hub's device-expiry timer, each sender's preferred chunk size) stays where it is
used - listing values nobody reads would be documentation theatre, not a contract.
Changing anything under 'crypto' or 'headers' changes the wire format: bump 'protocol' as well.
The marker is not a mere label - it is hashed into the KDF salt and info and into both pairing
proofs - so two peers on different versions derive different keys and fail each other's proof at
/handshake/verify. Each client also compares the marker the peer declares in that response, which
turns the same mismatch into a readable 'wrong version' message instead of a wrong-PIN error.

chunking._comment: The sealed packet is nonce || ciphertext || tag. The receiver takes chunkSize and count from inside the AAD, not from a header it has to trust: a header that is not authenticated can be rewritten by anything on the path, which is exactly how an early-finalize or a truncated file becomes invisible.

preferredChunkSizeBytes._comment: Tuning only, deliberately not asserted equal. Unifying them is a benchmark question (peak memory scales with chunk size x concurrency), and picking a number without measuring it is how the 1MB-to-4MB change ended up applied to one client out of four.

pairing._comment: Both ends implement this state machine separately, and every field that has been changed on one side only is in git history: the PIN entropy source (a7579df), the grace window (aca8139). The rate limiter exists on the hub as a window plus a block; Android previously counted failures forever.

session._comment: Idle-based with an absolute cap. Measuring from creation instead of last activity dropped sessions mid-transfer, which is why a hard ten-minute limit is not what either end should implement.
